meta.dataset: BSP public comparables: FY2023-FY2025 (latest available) SEC XBRL fundamentals for 31 listed peers across all six BSP portfolio sectors
meta.scope_note: Built for the whole BSP portfolio and its public rivals, not only Punctual Pros: residential home services (Punctual Pros), commercial electrical/energy (CET / NuWave), legal/BPO managed services (Frontline; CBIZ also covers Smith + Howard), lab distribution (Thomas Scientific), communications agencies, and apparel/DTC (Fair Harbor).
meta.method: CIKs resolved via sec.gov/files/company_tickers.json and EDGAR company search (for delisted or renamed filers: TopBuild 1633931, WNS 1356570, Patterson 891024, Interpublic 51644). Pulled data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts for every ticker with a declared User-Agent. For each concept, took annual-duration facts (340-380 days) from 10-K/20-F filings and kept the latest-filed value per fiscal year. Revenue concept priority: Revenues > RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax > IFRS Revenue. Operating income: OperatingIncomeLoss (IFRS ProfitLossFromOperatingActivities); where not reported (FTDR, KD), pre-tax income + interest expense. Net income: NetIncomeLoss (attributable to parent). D&A: DepreciationDepletionAndAmortization / DepreciationAndAmortization, else Depreciation + AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets. EBITDA approx = operating income + D&A, unadjusted, so impairments and deal costs stay in. dei:EntityNumberOfEmployees is rarely tagged, so headcount came from each 10-K/20-F Human Capital section, text-parsed from 95 downloaded filings. Fiscal year = calendar year of period end, except Jan/Feb year-ends (LULU, DLTH), which take the prior year. Latest-year growth = latest FY vs prior FY. Revenue/employee = latest FY revenue / year-end headcount. Sector values are medians across the comps listed for that sector; FIX counts in both residential and commercial.
meta.sources_summary: SEC XBRL companyfacts API (31 companies); SEC submissions API (filing lists, 10-K URLs, 15-12G/DEFM14A/DEFA14A/S-4 events); 95 primary 10-K/20-F documents for headcount, Ameresco FY2025 statements and WPP amortisation; Federal Reserve G.5A annual average GBP/USD rates (release of 2026-01-05) for WPP conversion.
caveats: All figures are GAAP/IFRS as reported and are not adjusted. EBITDA here is operating income + D&A, not company-defined Adjusted EBITDA. One-offs depress latest-year margins at AVTR (impairment), CROX (impairment), OMC (IPG deal costs), WPP (GBP 641M goodwill impairment) and TECH FY2025.
Headcount is year-end and often rounded ('approximately', 'more than', 'over'). PRIM = salaried + hourly; DLTH = full-time + part-time; STGW = full-time only.

Revenue per employee is not comparable across delivery models: offshore BPO runs about $18k-$35k, while pass-through distributors and project developers (PDCO, AMRC, FTDR, RVLV) run above $700k because of subcontractor or product costs.
WPP reports under IFRS in GBP. USD values use Fed annual average rates, growth is computed in GBP, and IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation inflates its EBITDA against US GAAP peers.

Some comps no longer file: TopBuild (acquired by QXO, 15-12G 2026-07-13), WNS (15-12G 2025-10-27), Patterson (take-private, 15-12G 2025-04-28) and Interpublic (acquired by Omnicom, 15-12G 2025-12-08). Their latest year is their last annual report. CBIZ (Grant Thornton affiliate, $55/share cash) and Bio-Techne (Merck KGaA) have pending acquisitions.
Ameresco's FY2025 10-K has no XBRL in companyfacts, so its FY2025 values were transcribed from the 10-K HTML.
Kyndryl (March FYE) and Bio-Techne (June FYE) include FY2026 as the latest year. IES (Sept FYE) and WNS (March FYE) are shown on their own fiscal calendars.
The mid-cap and large-cap public comps are 10-1000x the size of BSP's lower-middle-market platforms. Use them for direction (margin structure, productivity, growth cycle), not for valuation parity.
Allbirds now appears in EDGAR as 'Smartbird, Inc.' with the same CIK and ticker BIRD.

residential_home_services.what_this_implies_for_bsp: Public residential/trade comps grew a median 13.6% in their latest year at a 14.4% operating margin (13.1% multi-year average), but the set is bimodal: installers IBP/BLD are flat (+1.0%/+1.5%) at 13-15% margins while FIX (+29.5%) and LMB (+24.7%) are growing on non-residential/data-center mechanical work, so residential-only demand is closer to low single digits. For Punctual Pros, a mid-teens EBITDA margin (IBP 15.1%, BLD 17.8%, FTDR 24.2% on an asset-light warranty model) is the realistic mature target, and a technician-led service model should sit near the ~$285k-$400k revenue/employee band of IBP, BLD and FIX. Growth above the ~2-4% revenue CAGR of the installers will need density-building tuck-ins and service-agreement/recurring revenue, which is the lever the portal's territory model should prioritize.

commercial_electrical_energy.what_this_implies_for_bsp: Electrical/MEP and energy contractors are in a capex upcycle: median latest-year revenue growth is 16.9% (3-yr CAGR 16.8%) led by FIX, PWR, PRIM and IESC on data-center, grid and industrial work. Margins are structurally thin, with a median operating margin of 6.4% and approximate EBITDA margin of 11.2%, and only specialist/self-perform leaders (FIX 14.4%, IESC 11.4%, EME 10.1%) clear 10%; revenue per employee clusters tightly at ~$330k-$410k (Ameresco's $1.2M reflects pass-through project costs). For CET / NuWave, that implies a benchmark of roughly $330k-$410k revenue per field+office head and a 6-10% operating margin, with upside tied to mission-critical and service/maintenance mix rather than bid-hard GC work.

legal_bpo_managed_services.what_this_implies_for_bsp: BPO/managed-services comps posted a median 10.1% latest-year growth at a 12.6% operating margin and ~16.9% EBITDA margin, with TaskUs (+19.0%) and EXL (+13.6%) outgrowing Genpact (+6.6%) and WNS/Kyndryl flat. Revenue per employee is a delivery-model signal rather than a quality signal: offshore-heavy Genpact/EXL/TaskUs/WNS run $18k-$35k per head, while onshore professional-services models (CBIZ $290k, Kyndryl $210k) run 6-15x higher. For Frontline, an onshore US legal-services model should be benchmarked on the CBIZ-type revenue/employee and 8-12% operating margins, with offshore leverage the main path toward Genpact/EXL-style 15% margins; CBIZ's pending $55/share cash sale to a Grant Thornton affiliate is also a live valuation marker for Smith + Howard-type accounting platforms.

lab_distribution.what_this_implies_for_bsp: Lab and healthcare distribution is a low-growth, scale-margin business: median latest-year growth is 1.5% (3-yr CAGR 2.0%) and median operating margin 5.0% (7.4% multi-year average), with pure distributors HSIC and PDCO at ~4-5% while manufacturer-distributors TMO and TECH earn 17-21%. Revenue per employee for distributors runs roughly $485k-$865k (AVTR $485k, HSIC $527k, PDCO $864k), well above service businesses because product pass-through dominates revenue. For Thomas Scientific, a 4-7% EBITDA-to-revenue profile with $500k+ revenue per employee is the distribution benchmark, and margin expansion must come from proprietary/private-label mix and account penetration, since end-market volume growth is running near flat.

communications_agencies.what_this_implies_for_bsp: Agency holding companies are shrinking or flat on a like-for-like basis: median latest-year growth is 0.3%, with WPP down 8.1% in GBP, IPG down 1.8% before its sale, Stagwell +2.4%, and Omnicom's +10.1% driven by the IPG acquisition. Reported margins are distorted by impairments and deal costs (median latest operating margin 4.2% vs a 7.8% multi-year average), while normalized holding-company margins sit around 11-15% (OMC and IPG before 2025) and revenue per employee is ~$145k-$265k. For a BSP agency platform, benchmarks are roughly $190k-$265k revenue per employee and a 10-15% EBITDA margin, and growth has to come from specialist/earned-media and data capabilities because the category itself is ex-growth and consolidating.

apparel_dtc.what_this_implies_for_bsp: Apparel/DTC comps are bifurcated: the median latest-year growth is -1.5% and median operating margin 3.7%, but LULU (19.9%) and CROX (about 25-26% in FY2023-24, before its 2025 impairments) show what brand heat earns, while DLTH, RVLV and BIRD run -2% to 6% or deep losses. Allbirds (revenue down 19.7%, -52% operating margin, headcount 927 to 362 in two years) is the cautionary case for a single-category, DTC-first, sustainability-positioned footwear/apparel brand scaling stores too early. For Fair Harbor, the benchmark is roughly $275k-$500k revenue per employee and a positive high-single-digit EBITDA margin before scaling retail, with wholesale/marketplace mix (as Crocs and Revolve show) preferable to heavy owned-store build-outs.

meta.financial_picture: Across 31 public peers, the BSP portfolio splits into three economic regimes. (1) Construction and trades (CET / NuWave and Punctual Pros) is the growth engine: commercial electrical/MEP comps compounded revenue at a median 16.8% from FY2023 to FY2025, versus 8.4% for the residential and trade set. The trades still have thin margins, with a median operating margin of 6.4% for commercial electrical, 11.2% approximate EBITDA, and only specialists like FIX (14.4%), IESC (11.4%) and EME (10.1%) at or above 10%, so contractor value creation comes from mix (service, mission-critical) more than price. Residential comps show the split Punctual Pros faces: pure residential installers IBP and TopBuild grew only 1-1.5% in FY2025 at 13-15% operating margins, while the fast growers (FIX, LMB) are leaning on non-residential work. Frontdoor's 24% approximate EBITDA margin on about $1.03M revenue per employee shows the value of a subscription and asset-light contractor-network model in home services. (2) Services and people businesses (Frontline, Smith + Howard, the agency holding) are priced on productivity per head. Offshore BPO earns 12-15% operating margins at only $18k-$35k revenue per employee, while onshore professional services (CBIZ $290k, Kyndryl $210k) earn 3-9%. So a US-heavy legal or accounting platform should expect CBIZ-like economics unless it adds offshore leverage. Agencies are ex-growth (median +0.3%, WPP -8.1% in GBP) and consolidating (Omnicom absorbed Interpublic, taking headcount from 74,900 to about 120,000), so a BSP agency asset has to win on specialist growth rather than category tailwind. (3) Product businesses (Thomas Scientific, Fair Harbor) are scale-and-mix stories. Lab distribution grows at a median 1.5% with 4-5% operating margins for pure distributors (HSIC, PDCO), against 17-21% for manufacturers (TMO, TECH), so private-label and proprietary content are the margin lever for Thomas Scientific. Apparel/DTC is the most dispersed sector: LULU earns about 20% operating margin, but Duluth and Allbirds show negative margins and shrinking revenue, and Allbirds went from 927 to 362 employees in two years. For Fair Harbor, capital discipline around retail expansion matters more than top-line speed. Finally, M&A activity among the comps (QXO/TopBuild, the WNS and Patterson take-outs in 2025, Omnicom/Interpublic, Grant Thornton affiliate/CBIZ at $55 cash, Merck KGaA/Bio-Techne) signals active strategic and sponsor demand in four of BSP's six sectors, which supports exit optionality for the portfolio.

data_gaps: This track only pulls public-company fundamentals. Private-company techniques A-E from the research template were not run here: EDGAR full-text/Form D/BDC schedules, SBA PPP, state registries/UCC/OSHA/courts, trade rankings, and credit ratings. None of their findings are in this file; they belong to the per-portfolio-company tracks.

No listed pure-play residential plumbing/HVAC service consolidator was available: ARS, Service Experts, Wrench Group, Apex and Sila are private. Residential comps are proxies (installers, warranty, commercial MEP).
No public pure-play US legal managed-services provider was found. Genpact, EXL, TaskUs and WNS are general BPO, and legal process outsourcing is a small share of their revenue.
No public pure-play lab-supply distributor near Thomas Scientific's scale was found. Fisher Scientific sits inside TMO and VWR inside AVTR; neither is broken out as distribution-only in XBRL.
dei:EntityNumberOfEmployees is tagged by only a few filers (LMB, Genpact to FY2024, Kyndryl to FY2024), so headcount relies on text parsing.
Company-defined Adjusted EBITDA (the figure lenders and sponsors use) is not in XBRL and was not pulled.
WPP FY2024-FY2025 D&A was assembled from 20-F text and IFRS tags and includes some intangible impairment.
next_pulls: Add Adjusted EBITDA from each comp's 8-K earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) to replace the GAAP operating income + D&A approximation.

Add valuation: EV/EBITDA and EV/Revenue from share count (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding), net debt from balance-sheet XBRL, and a price feed. Use announced deal multiples (CBIZ $55/share, Bio-Techne/Merck KGaA, QXO/TopBuild, Patterson, WNS) as precedent transactions.

Add segment-level XBRL (StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis) for the residential segments of EME/FIX, Fisher-channel distribution inside TMO, and VWR distribution inside AVTR to get closer pure-play benchmarks.

Add smaller comps: Bowman Consulting, NV5 and Willdan for energy services; Legalzoom and CS Disco for legal tech; Mister Car Wash/ServiceMaster-type service models; Vera Bradley, Lands' End and Figs for DTC apparel.
Refresh quarterly from 10-Qs (last-twelve-months revenue and margins) and re-run when FY2026 10-Ks land in Feb-Mar 2027.
Run techniques A-E (BDC schedules, PPP, UCC, rankings) for each BSP portfolio company and place their implied revenue/EBITDA against these sector medians.
